questions.q: Which Indian private company was first to put a rocket into orbit, and when?
questions.do: Tap Skyroot Aerospace under Who does what, or read the timeline in What changed since 2020.
questions.a: Skyroot Aerospace: its Vikram-1 reached a 450 km orbit on 18 July 2026, on its first try. That made India the third country, after the USA and China, where a private company has launched to orbit.

questions.q: How fast must India's space economy grow every year to go from $8.4 billion in 2022 to $44 billion in 2033?
questions.do: Press Goal pace on The road to $44 billion chart and read Pace the goal needs.
questions.a: About 16.2% a year, every year for eleven years. At that pace the industry doubles roughly every 4.6 years.

questions.q: Which startup satellite can see through monsoon clouds and at night, and why?
questions.do: Tap GalaxEye and read What it means for people.
questions.a: GalaxEye's Drishti (launched 3 May 2026) carries a radar. Radar sends its own radio waves and times the echoes, so it does not need sunlight and passes through clouds. It also carries an ordinary camera.

questions.q: Startups raised about $200 million in 2025. Roughly what share is that of the Department of Space's yearly budget?
questions.do: Look at the bars in The money going in.
questions.a: About ₹1,740 crore against ₹13,706 crore for the Department of Space in 2026–27: roughly 13%. Startup money is growing fast (it was $43 million in 2021) but the government is still by far the biggest spender.

questions.q: What did the government change in June 2020 that started this whole story?
questions.do: Read the first entry in What changed since 2020.
questions.a: It set up IN-SPACe, which gives private companies permission to build and launch. Before that, almost everything India sent to space was built and launched by ISRO.
